candidate.title: AGO-CLIP
candidate.scope: Architecture of the single AGO-CLIP row in the supplied Illumina poster, from an AGO–miRNA–target RNA complex through 4SU incorporation, 365 nm UV crosslinking, RNase T1 digestion, T4 RNA ligation, proteinase K, RNA extraction, and reverse transcription to cDNA. The matched primary implementation is C. elegans ALG-1 iPAR-CLIP modified for miRNA–target chimera production. “AGO-CLIP” is the target name; modified iPAR-CLIP identifies this supported implementation within that broader family, without asserting identical preparation for every AGO-CLIP assay. The left “Map miRNA binding to AGO sites in C. elegans” icon explains purpose rather than a separate processing branch. Adjacent iCLIP, BrdU-CLIP, and PIP-Seq rows, other catalogue applications, and no-added-ligase reactions discussed in the paper are not alternative target workflows in this row. The figure ends at cDNA and abstracts subsequent sequencing-library details.

states.label: cDNA representing recovered AGO-associated RNAs
features: The final blue line is labeled cDNA and is produced by the arrow labeled Reverse transcription.
DNA is the readout carrier copied from extracted RNA; a miRNA–target RNA junction can therefore be represented as a contiguous sequence in one cDNA molecule.
The paper distinguishes nonchimeric miRNA/AGO-site reads from chimeric reads that directly associate a particular miRNA sequence with its target fragment.
T-to-C read conversions support PAR-CLIP crosslink evidence; a conversion alone does not establish miRNA identity at a target site.

Chimera capture is incomplete and may favor some interactions. The authors propose greater recovery for stable and well-expressed interactions; read counts are not established here as calibrated interaction strength, and binding does not by itself demonstrate repression.
No barcode, sequencing-adapter design, PCR, or distinct alternative product branch is drawn in this AGO-CLIP row.

operations.label: T4-RNA ligase
operations.description: The depicted ligation block converts AGO-associated RNA segments into connected miRNA–target RNA products. The matched primary resolves its compressed input interface: AGO immunopurification selects AGO-associated RNA from RNase-treated material, and a PNK variant prepares RNA ends before T4 RNA ligase acts. These consequential prerequisites are included within this block’s interpretation, not asserted to be separately drawn operations (c2).
operations.mechanism: T4 RNA ligase joins the 3′ hydroxyl of a full-length miRNA to the prepared 5′ end of its target RNA fragment. PNK-mediated phosphorylation leaves target 3′ ends blocked, suppressing circularization. The ligase and PNK are catalysts rather than sequenced substrates; the selected AGO complex holds the RNA partners during ligation.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the association between a miRNA and its AGO-bound target fragment into a covalent RNA junction that can survive protein removal and be copied into a single cDNA/read. The primary’s ligation samples also contain products attributable to endogenous ligation, so the depicted T4 addition does not establish an exclusive origin for every chimera or complete recovery of all interactions.
